slides.subtitle: One-hop sibling and inverse-blocks gating, at zero GraphQL cost

slides.heading: What prune actually removes
lines: It removes a long-closed issue from the project board only — the GitHub issue stays intact.
What is lost is the board item: its Workflow State and Claim values go with it.
So the predicate must fail closed on every closed item another reader still needs.
Two of the five relationship edges were ungated.

slides.heading: sibling-edge
lines: A closed item sharing an own-repo parent with an OPEN item is held.
One hop only — a sibling's siblings are not walked.
board.ts:6237 — the gate sits before the age check, so it binds once the item ages out.

slides.heading: blocks-edge
lines: GitHub exposes no inverse blocks connection.
But an open item's CLOSED blockers are exactly the closed items that block something open.
The inverse falls out of the forward edge — so no nested connection is added, and the query costs the same.
A truncated blocker list on the open side fails closed for every candidate.

slides.title:
Retention is now reported
on every path
slides.subtitle: An over-tight rule is only visible if the tally always prints

captions.text: GH-1883 closed the last two ungated relationship edges in board prune.
Pruning removes the board item, not the issue — Workflow State and Claim go with it.
That is one-way, so the predicate has to fail closed on anything another reader still needs.
sibling-edge: a closed item is held while it shares an own-repo parent with an open one.
Exactly one hop — a sibling's siblings are not walked.
blocks-edge: GitHub has no inverse blocks connection to read.
The inverse falls out of the forward edge, so nothing new is queried and the cost is unchanged.
Run live against this board: 818 closed items, none prunable today.
17 held by sibling-edge and 3 by blocks-edge — reasons that did not exist before this change.
Measured with RALPH_GQL_COST=1: the GraphQL document is byte-identical. 16 pages, 48 points, before and after.
And the retention tally now prints on every path, not only when there is nothing to prune.
